title: Holistic Apportionment Orchestrator for per-route/model/customer cost & latency
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build a resilient, auditable orchestration service that computes deterministic cost and latency attributions for every inference request across three dimensions: route, model variant, and customer (tenant). This service — the Holistic Apportionment Orchestrator (HAO) — will ingest enriched request traces and runtime telemetry (token counts, KV cache hits, GPU kernel footprints, batching records, retry/fallback traces) and emit per-request allocation records and aggregated rollups for downstream billing, per-route dashboards, and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: 1) HAO produces per-request allocation records that include: tokens_charged, model_variant, route_id, customer_id, compute_ms, storage_ms, cache_hit_ratio, batching_delay_ms, and apportionment_reason_code. 2) Aggregates match offline economic model within 1% on synthetic workloads and within 3% on sampled production. 3) Service supports schema evolution (v1->v2) without data loss and has a migration plan. 4) Latency attribution traces can be joined to trace IDs emitted by serving runtime. 5) Rollout gated behind canary with 1% of requests and rollback toggle in Console.
design_decisions:
- We will use a hybrid approach: deterministic token-level apportioner for exact requests (fast path) and sampled probabilistic rollout for heavy aggregates (heavy path) to bound CPU cost.
- Attribution joins will be performed using a time-bounded streaming join keyed by request_id; this avoids expensive broad joins on tenant/model.
- To minimize coordination, HAO will emit idempotent allocation records (write-once semantics using request_id+attempt).
- Use protobuf v2 for allocation record schema to ensure compactness and forward/backward compatibility.
- We will compute 'effective_compute_ms' by combining kernel-level footprints (from runtime) with batching_delay attribution (split pro-rata by tokens or explicit batch-affinity when available).
implementation_notes:
- Stream sources: enriched request events (kafka topic: requests.enriched.v2), runtime telemetry (kafka: runtime.metrics), cache events (kafka: cache.hits), and billing_cost_factors (s3:cost-factors/daily).
- Core implementation in Go as a microservice with a Flink-compatible streaming layer for joins and windowed rollups. Lightweight path for per-request synchronous enrichment (GRPC) to support Console's diagnostic UI.
- Backpressure strategy: when joins lag >30s, switch heavy aggregation to sampling mode and mark emitted records with sampling_factor.
- Storage: per-request allocation records written to parquet in s3 (partitioned by date/customer) and an operational write to ClickHouse for near-real-time dashboards.
- Observability: emit metrics for join-lag, allocation_delta (compared to baseline cheap estimator), sampling_rate, and apportioner_error_rate.
milestones: Canary rollout (1% traffic) and verify dashboards
Full rollout and switch downstream pipelines to HAO outputs
comments: 2025-12-05: Initial PRD reviewed by PM (Jonah Reed) and Research (Dr. Mei Wong). PM asked for explicit rollback strategy and per-customer opt-out; added to design.
2026-01-12: Prototype using in-memory join shows 20% lower CPU than naive join by leveraging request affinity. Logged micro-benchmarks in: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hao/pulls/12
2026-01-28: Architecture review with Infra. Recommendation: move heavy aggregations to a separate Flink cluster to avoid head-of-line impact on low-latency enrichment path.
2026-02-02: Security review acknowledged; no PII in allocation records, but tenant IDs considered sensitive — storage access restricted via RBAC and KMS encryption (ticketed separately).

2026-02-08: QA discovered edge-case where retried requests produced duplicate allocation records. Implemented idempotency by request_id+attempt dedupe in staging (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/hao/pull/34).

2026-02-13: Canary kickoff (1% traffic). Early metrics: allocation_delta against legacy ledger shows +2.1% variance on windy workloads (short sequences with many retries). Created follow-up subtask to refine retry attribution.
2026-02-15: PR for ClickHouse schema and parquet writer merged. Next steps: expand canary to 5% and run daily reconciliation job for 7 days before wider rollout.
next_steps: 1) Complete heavy-aggregation Flink job and verify cost (CPU) under full production ingestion. 2) Implement per-customer opt-out and compliance hooks. 3) Extend test harness to generate edge-case trace patterns (mass retries, long KV cache warmups). 4) Increase canary to 5% pending reconciliation results.
notes: This ticket consolidates earlier cost/latency decomposition efforts into a single orchestrator focused on explainability and deterministic apportionment. Avoids building a new billing sink — initial output is compatible with existing billing ingestion formats.
